text:
priya: quick question — I'm working through rollout metadata and wondered whether provenance should carry both an immutable build_hash + a materialization origin field? thinking about rollback determinism vs payload size.

alex: +1 for build_hash. we need something clients can assert. origin is useful but can be large (s3 path, registry ref) — maybe keep origin as optional string. :thinking:

jasper: we also need to consider live pins: if a model is pinned to a version, the pin record should include a short fingerprint (8-12 hex) and a stable TTL so autoscaler can evict if lease expires. otherwise stale pins block capacity.

maria: question: do we standardize on hex fingerprint or use content-hash (sha256) in metadata? fingerprints are smaller for logs and UI.

alex: propose dual fields: fingerprint_short and content_sha256. short for human/fast checks, full sha256 for authoritative comparisons. both strings.

priya: that seems reasonable. also need to decide where rollout hints live — client-visible metadata vs control-plane-only. e.g., 'preferred_variant' and 'fallback_chain' for smart routing.

sam: routing wants cheap hints. we should expose preferred_variant (string) and fallback_chain (comma-separated list) in the pin record. clients can ignore if they only care about strict pin.

jasper: tradeoff: making fallback_chain public ties clients to internal variant names. maybe expose opaque variant IDs and a small TTL-propagation policy.

maria: also, can we avoid storing heavy URLs in pin records? Suggest storing origin_kind (enum: registry, s3, local) + origin_ref (short ref or id). full URLs can be kept in an append-only artifact store referenced by id.

priya: agreed. sketch of candidate metadata (we can iterate):
```
build_hash: "b6f9c2a4"
fingerprint_short: "b6f9c2a4"
content_sha256: "2e7d..."
origin_kind: "registry"
origin_ref: "reg-2026-03-05-42"
pin_ttl_seconds: "86400"
preferred_variant: "v1-small"
fallback_chain: "v1-small,v1-medium,v0-compat"
provenance_note: "trained-with-latest-tokenizer"
```

alex: one more: include a 'materialized_at' timestamp and 'materialized_by' (job id) for debugging. keep all fields strings to simplify storage and indexing.

sam: for rollback safety we need an authoritative 'immutable_id' that maps to the runtime artifact. content_sha256 works, but we should also add 'immutable_kind' (e.g., container, model-file) to avoid collisions.

maria: ops: when pin_ttl expires, do we auto-evict or mark stale and emit alert? prefer mark-stale + housekeeping job, because auto-evict could break quick rollbacks.

jasper: mark-stale sounds safer. housekeeping can be a lower-priority background job that frees capacity after another threshold. record 'stale_since' when TTL lapses.

priya: ok agreed on flow: TTL lapses -> mark_stale=true + stale_since -> housekeeping window (configurable) before eviction. update UI and telemetry.

deploy-bot: deploy report: pin service image v1.14 deployed to staging at 3305001300 — pin_ttl default set to 7d for new pins. :rocket:

priya: follow-ups: 1) I'll draft a compact JSON schema for this and share. 2) need clear migration plan for existing pins (backfill content_sha256 and fingerprint_short). 3) define limits for origin_ref length.

alex: for migration, run a batching job that computes sha256 for existing artifacts and sets fingerprint_short; mark migration_status on the pin until done. keep backward compat.

maria: I'll add telemetry counters for stale_pin_count and avg_pin_ttl to SLO dashboard.

jasper: tiny nit — use snake_case to match other metadata. also include schema_version field so we can evolve without breaking older clients.

priya: good call. I'll include schema_version in the draft. thanks everyone — I'll post the RFC follow-up with the JSON schema and a suggested backfill plan. :white_check_mark:
